ranking_method.stage_1: Subtract exact requirement-level support and recompute corrected single-step primitive leverage.
ranking_method.stage_2: Recheck coarse primitive closure against actual implemented predicate/capability surfaces; primitive-name presence alone is insufficient.
ranking_method.stage_3: Regroup actual closable rows by shared receipt/scenario and rank by unlocked case count, shared receipt density, reusable predicate density, then new semantic surface size.
ranking_method.routing_rule: planned_test_id membership remains routing metadata and is not requirement-level support.

incremental_surface: Interpret ToolAdapterCapability boundary declarations as bounded capability evidence.
Bind CaptureDiagnostic observed assertions to their declared ToolInvocation, ToolExecution, and ToolResult slots.
Require baseline invocation/execution/result objects to agree with the declared adapter-visible boundaries.
Preserve proposal optionality and absence of implicit allow decision.
Keep completed/success lifecycle and result evidence separate from external Effect truth.

tool_lifecycle.reason_not_selected: Lower primitive leverage and smaller tight cluster.

verifier_report.reason_not_selected: Lower primitive leverage and smaller tight core than the selected 10-case baseline adapter cluster.

selected_cluster.selection_reason: prim.adapter.capture has the highest corrected single-step leverage at 97. After actual-capability recheck, tool-adapter-baseline.json provides the largest dependency-closed tight cluster: ten requirements on one receipt. The receipt explicitly carries one ToolAdapterCapability, one invocation/execution/result chain, and three slot-bound CaptureDiagnostics. Existing lifecycle/reference predicates cover the object relationships, while the new surface is concentrated in bounded adapter capability/diagnostic interpretation. Same-receipt rows requiring receipt.multi or claim.strength are excluded.
